name: Qt Code Intelligence (Python, QML, C++)
description: VS Code-style editor views for Qt developers: Ctrl+Click / F12 to go to definition, hover, completion, diagnostics and semantic colors for Python (basedpyright, auto-selects the project's interpreter), QML (qmlls) and C/C++ (clangd). Works on files of other machines too, over SSH.

settings.title: Python interpreter
settings.description: Force one interpreter for every project. Empty (recommended): pick per project like VS Code (.vscode setting, project venv with the highest Python, then the highest installed Python).

settings.title: Python type checking
settings.description: How strictly Pyright checks types: off (default, like VS Code's Pylance: only syntax and unresolved imports), basic, standard, strict. Takes effect after restarting the language server.

settings.title: Use project environments
settings.description: on (default): pick the project's own venv / conda env, .vscode/settings.json and pyrightconfig like VS Code. Pyright then runs that environment's python to read its library paths, so only open projects you trust. off: use installed Pythons only.

settings.title: Pyright language server
settings.description: Path to basedpyright's or pyright's langserver.index.js. Empty: %LOCALAPPDATA%\orca-qt-lsp, then the global npm folder.

settings.title: Node.js
settings.description: Node used to run Pyright. Empty: node on PATH.

settings.title: Qt bin folder
settings.description: Kit bin folder holding qmlls (e.g. C:\Qt\6.12.0\mingw_64\bin). Empty: newest Qt under C:\Qt or ~/Qt.

settings.title: qmlls
settings.description: Path to qmlls. Empty: from the Qt bin folder.

settings.title: clangd
settings.description: Path to clangd. Empty: Qt Creator's, LLVM's, then PATH.

settings.title: Extra compiler globs for clangd
settings.description: clangd only queries compilers from known toolchain folders (Qt, LLVM, Visual Studio, MSYS2, /usr/bin…) for system include paths, never one inside the project. Add other trusted compiler paths here as globs, separated by commas.

settings.title: Extra SSH hosts
settings.description: Usually empty: when the open file is not on this machine the plugin searches every host in ~/.ssh/config by itself (read-only, in parallel) and remembers the one that has the project. Use the machine button at the bottom of the editor to pick or type a host for a project. Add hosts here only if they are not in ~/.ssh/config (user@host), separated by commas.

settings.title: Find files on SSH hosts automatically
settings.description: on (default): when the open file is not on this machine, look for it read-only on every host in ~/.ssh/config (key login only, at most 40 hosts, files of 64 bytes or more) and start the agent on the host that has it. off: only use the host picked with the machine button.

settings.title: Remote project folders
settings.description: Optional: project folders on the remote hosts to search (separate with ;). Searched anyway: folders used before, Orca's workspaces on that host (when Orca is installed there), then the home folder.

settings.title: ssh
settings.description: Path to the ssh program. Empty: the system OpenSSH.

settings.title: Remote node path
settings.description: Optional: Node.js on the remote hosts when it is not on the SSH PATH (e.g. /home/me/.nvm/versions/node/v20.11.0/bin/node).
